headline: LONDON COPPER BIDDING WAR LOOMS AS LME STOCKS PLUNGE 14% — COMEX HITS ALL-TIME RECORD 675K TONNES; CASH-TO-3-MONTH SPREAD WIDENS TO 5-YEAR HIGH
snippet: LME on-warrant copper inventories have fallen 14% since end-July with 65,400 tonnes earmarked for imminent withdrawal, pushing the cash-to-three-month spread to its widest backwardation in five years — a structure that forced emergency LME intervention in the 2021 nickel squeeze and is now forming in copper. COMEX copper inventories simultaneously hit an all-time record of 675,185 tonnes as tariff-anxious US traders pre-position ahead of proposed 15-30% import duties effective January 2027. The dual divergence — LME depleting while COMEX builds — exposes London short positions to an acute warehouse bidding war with no precedent under the current tariff-distorted structure: shorts facing delivery obligations in London cannot easily cover from COMEX stocks without incurring the tariff premium. For junior copper explorers, the physical market is pricing scarcity NOW — not in three years when new mines could theoretically respond — and LME backwardation of this magnitude has historically preceded the sector re-rating events that drive explorers' best relative performance.

headline: STANMORE RESOURCES SEALS US$145M MORANBAH SOUTH DEAL — 724MT PREMIUM HARD COKING COAL ADJACENT TO EAGLE DOWNS AS BOWEN BASIN CONSOLIDATION ACCELERATES
snippet: Stanmore Resources has agreed to acquire 100% of the Moranbah South tenements in Queensland's Bowen Basin from Exxaro Resources for US$105-145 million, completing a two-step deal in which Exxaro first exercised pre-emptive rights to buy Anglo American's 50% interest in the Moranbah South JV — triggered by Anglo's sale of its Australian coal assets to Dhilmar QLD Ltd. — before immediately selling the full 100% to Stanmore. The Moranbah South tenements contain 724 million tonnes of measured and indicated premium hard coking coal in the Goonyella Middle Seam, immediately adjacent to Stanmore's Eagle Downs and Isaac Downs Extension projects, with potential for resource access through existing Eagle Downs mine infrastructure. Completion is targeted before end Q4 2026 subject to FIRB, ACCC, and ministerial approval. The deal confirms that world-class Bowen Basin metallurgical coal assets continue to trade at scale among serious operators — and that the steel industry's ongoing demand for premium-quality coking coal is sustaining M&A economics even in a decarbonisation-narrative environment.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,388-$4,358 SUPPORT AS CPI WEEK OPENS; HOT NFP LOCKS RATE-HIKE ODDS AT 60-66% WITH THURSDAY AUGUST CPI THE DECISIVE INPUT
snippet: Gold steadied near $4,430 through the Labor Day holiday session after August nonfarm payrolls — 162,000 vs. 56,000 consensus — erased a portion of the week's Treasury-buyback-driven gains and pushed CME FedWatch September rate-hike probability to 60-66%. The $4,388-$4,358 zone has held as the critical technical floor through two tests this week; bulls require a CPI reading at or below 3.4% on Thursday September 10 to cement a September 16 Fed hold and unlock the next leg toward $4,600-$4,800 — while a reading above 3.5% would reanimate the hike case that drove gold's 21% drawdown from its January 2026 record at $5,589. The NFP-vs-treasury-buyback dynamic crystallises the core tension of September's gold market: the structural debasement bid (US Treasury purchasing its own long-dated bonds to cap the back end of the curve) and the monetary tightening bid are operating simultaneously, and the CPI print will temporarily resolve which force prevails over the next two weeks — without eliminating either.

headline: SILVER AT $65.55 — 59% ABOVE YEAR-AGO BUT 46% OFF JANUARY'S $121.79 COMEX PEAK; CHINA'S STRATEGIC RECLASSIFICATION SETS A STRUCTURAL FLOOR
snippet: Silver fell to $65.55 per troy ounce on September 7, down 0.9% on the session as the dollar strengthened following the hot August NFP report, extending its 46% correction from January 29's COMEX record of $121.79. Despite the pullback, silver is 59% above its year-ago price — one of the strongest one-year performances in the metal's modern trading history — and two structural supports distinguish the current setup from a simple rate-hike risk selloff: China reclassified silver as a strategic material on January 1, 2026, imposing export licence requirements that constrain global refined silver supply from a country that accounts for an estimated 60-70% of global refined silver exports; and the silver market is tracking toward its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit in 2026, with investment demand running approximately 95 million ounces above production. At the current gold-to-silver ratio above 65-to-1, silver offers meaningful leverage to any gold price recovery while the structural supply-demand imbalance provides a demand floor that is independent of the Fed's September rate decision.

headline: URANIUM SPOT REBOUNDS TO $82/LB (+8% IN SEPTEMBER) AS KAZATOMPROM SIGNALS 20% DOWNFLEX BELOW ALREADY-REDUCED 77M-LB GUIDANCE
snippet: Spot uranium has recovered to $82 per pound in September 2026, an 8.05% gain on the month, as compounding supply-side signals force a market reassessment of the deficit's depth. Kazatomprom — responsible for roughly 23% of global primary uranium supply — has signalled it intends to exercise its 'downflex' option to cut 2026 production by up to 20% below its already-reduced nominal guidance of approximately 77 million pounds U3O8, implying actual 2026 output could fall to 61-62 million pounds — a level that, combined with Cameco's McArthur River production shortfall covered in Tuesday's earlier batch, leaves the global supply side of the uranium market significantly tighter than official 2026 guidance figures implied at the start of the year. World Nuclear Association demand projections (uranium requirements to more than double by 2040) are based on supply models that missed five key production cuts announced since June 2026, meaning the true supply gap is wider than official models show and the spot uranium recovery toward $82/lb has fundamental justification independent of the rate cycle.

headline: CAML SHAREHOLDERS APPROVE CYGNUS METALS ACQUISITION; CHIBOUGAMAU COPPER-GOLD SCHEME MEETING SEPTEMBER 18 — DEAL CLOSES OCTOBER 5
snippet: Central Asia Metals (LSE: CAML) shareholders voted overwhelmingly in favour of the all-share acquisition of Cygnus Metals at an Extraordinary General Meeting held September 4, 2026, authorising directors to allot new shares for a deal valued at approximately A$232 million ($166M USD), giving legacy CAML shareholders 70% of the combined entity. The final Cygnus shareholder scheme meeting is scheduled for September 18, with court implementation September 23 and a deal close date of October 5. Cygnus's principal asset — the Chibougamau copper-gold project in central Québec — adds 6.4 million tonnes of M&I resources at approximately 3% copper equivalent (grown 78% under Cygnus management) across an 18-kilometre strike length with a refurbishable brownfield mill already on site. CAML's move from a Kazakhstan-only asset base into Canadian copper is the template transaction that the current market is rewarding: development-stage copper in stable jurisdictions with existing infrastructure is trading at premiums that make all-share acquisitions structurally attractive — the Cygnus exchange ratio priced the project at a level that would have been impossible to justify one year ago.

headline: SPROTT MONEY/VERMEULEN: GOLD SEPTEMBER — SELLOFF OR BREAKOUT? $4,388 SUPPORT KEY; FIBONACCI LONG-TERM TARGET $7,900-$8,000 IF CORRECTION HOLDS
snippet: Technical analyst Chris Vermeulen, featured in Sprott Money's September preview, identifies the $4,388-$4,358 support zone as the critical test for gold bulls through the CPI-FOMC event window this week and next. His long-term Fibonacci analysis places a post-correction gold target at $7,900-$8,000 — conditional on the current drawdown from January's $5,589 high establishing a durable bottom, which Vermeulen says will be confirmed if gold holds above $4,200 through September 16 regardless of whether the Fed hikes or holds. Two signals anchor his constructive read: miners (GDX) breaking through significant prior highs while gold itself has not yet cleared equivalent resistance — a leading indicator that has preceded every sustainable gold advance in the last decade — and the structural debasement bid that operates independently of Fed decisions. Vermeulen's framework provides retail investors with a specific falsification test for September: a weekly close below $4,200 is the signal to reduce exposure and wait for a lower re-entry, rather than averaging down through what could be a deeper correction toward $3,800-$4,000.

headline: NdPr SLIPS 2.5% IN SEPTEMBER AS HEAVY RARE EARTHS SURGE 6-7% — REE COMPLEX DIVERGES AHEAD OF NOVEMBER 27 CHINA EXPORT CONTROL RESET
snippet: Neodymium and praseodymium metals — the benchmark NdPr alloy — have each fallen approximately 2.5% in September 2026 while heavy rare earth oxides diverge sharply: holmium oxide is up 7.14% and erbium oxide has gained 6.16% on the month. The divergence reflects distinct supply-chain vulnerabilities: NdPr from Inner Mongolia's Bayan Obo deposit faces less immediate constraint than heavy REEs (dysprosium, terbium, holmium) that derive from ion-adsorption clay deposits in Jiangxi and Guangdong provinces, where China's export licensing regime can be applied with more surgical precision. With China's enhanced export control suspension expiring November 27, 2026 — approximately 80 days from now — industrial buyers of both light and heavy REEs are in active last-buy mode, and the September price divergence signals that the market assigns a higher tightening probability to heavy REEs than to light REEs under the restored control regime. Western processing capacity holders — Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU) and USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) — remain the primary beneficiaries of this dynamic as buyers seek to pre-position non-Chinese supply ahead of the licensing reset.
